recipe.notes: Score: raw cosine similarity in [-1, 1] (float32) of the projector-transformed states at the two marker tokens (embed_token 151670 per document, rerank_token 151671 for the query); no sigmoid, softmax, temperature or scale. use_activation cannot change it (the token_embed pooler has no head: vllm/model_executor/models/jina.py:67-73; the score is the cosine of the projected marker embeddings), so the false pin on the wire and in serve.pooler_config is inert -- kept only for the rerank family's uniform declaration.  The model is listwise: one query's whole candidate set travels in one prompt, built SERVER-SIDE by vLLM's native Python builder (JinaRankingIOProcessorMixin.format_docs_prompts_func), which is byte-identical to the checkpoint's modeling.py (measured when the recipe was written; re-verified at the v0.31.0 tag). NO chat-template file ships on purpose (serve.chat_template: null): this architecture's prompt builder is Python, not a jinja template, and vLLM never consults a chat template on the Jina path; the warn-and-concatenate fallback belongs to template-driven io processors.  The declared pair template mirrors that builder's 1-vs-1 render byte for byte (stage 1's render check proves it); the N-passage listwise prompt is the engine's own builder with the same frame.  The query appears twice (the intro line and the <query> block): the declared pair shape spans it twice. The pair fit binds on overflow only (an under-budget pair ships whole); the rerank client settles the shared query span once per call -- whenever the query exceeds its share (query_max_tokens 512) it ships at it, recorded once in the census under the doc id <query> -- and fills both spans with the settled query, exactly the checkpoint's single truncation. Per-shape query cap (whether query_max_tokens applies): the reference truncates queries at 512 tokens (the checkpoint's max_query_length, decode-back, modeling.py _truncate_texts) -- query_max_tokens 512 declares exactly it.  Per-document cap: the reference truncates every document at 2048 tokens (the checkpoint's max_doc_length, the same _truncate_texts) -- document_max_tokens 2048 declares exactly it: the client cuts each document over 2048 tokens to 2048 on its content span and records the cut (document_share), so no document reaches the model longer than the checkpoint reads it.  Budget: max_tokens 3219 = the measured fixed frame (147 tokens, empty content, pinned tokenizer) + query_max_tokens 512 TWICE (the query spans the prompt two times -- the intro line and the <query> block -- so the budget reserves both copies) + 2048 (the checkpoint's per-document cap); 147 + 2*512 + 2048 = 3219 is the checkpoint's own worst-case 1-vs-1 prompt, and every pair within its per-text caps (query <= 512, document <= 2048) renders under this budget uncut.  The client's document cut therefore binds at the 2048-token cap, below the pair budget's 3072 - 2*q_tokens (q = the fitted query's tokens) for every query within its share.  The rerank client cuts client-side and never sends the engine's per-text request caps (no max_tokens_per_doc, max_tokens_per_query or truncate_prompt_tokens: rcp-ndcg/src/rcp_ndcg/inference/clients/rerank.py module docstring); the checkpoint truncates by decode-back, the client by an offset cut on the content span, so a document over 2048 tokens is cut by both, each its own way -- the declared over_cap_cut_differs: the harness reports such a pair (the client's processing record names the document_share cut) instead of gating it.  The instruction is none (the paper sends the bare query), and empty_doc: omit_zero_blank declares the paper's own rule (an empty OR whitespace-only document scores exactly 0.0 without a model call; the reference's `if d.strip()` is the same rule), while empty_query: send matches the reference, which formats any query. Listwise depth: one listwise request carries the whole candidate set, and the engine's window is max_model_len 131072; with the 147-token frame and the 512-token query reserved twice, a cap-length (2048-token) document costs ~2063 prompt tokens, so a request of 150 such documents (307,200 tokens) cannot fit -- the pairs files keep the depth at 4 or fewer. A default depth field is not expressible in the recipe schema today (a product gap; a listwise caller must split the candidate set), and the wave's pairs stay well under the window.  EQUIVALENCE HAS TWO REGIMES.  (1) Single-block (fewer than 125 documents AND residual capacity 131072 - 2*q_len strictly above 2048 after every document -- the flush test is <=): POST /rerank with the whole candidate set equals the paper's scores up to bf16 numerics (vLLM's own tolerance 0.01; the gate is |delta| <= 0.01 on cosine, median Kendall tau >= 0.98).  (2) The paper's NORMAL regime at depth 150: the checkpoint's rerank() blocks documents -- simulated with modeling.py's own constants, 150 cap-length (2048-token) documents block as [63, 63, 24] (the token-capacity flush binds at ~63 docs/block), short documents (<= ~1018 tokens) reach the 125-doc cap first ([125, 25]); each block gets its own query embed, the block weight is max((1+cos)/2) over its documents, the FINAL query embed is the block-weighted average and every document is scored against it in float32.  No single /rerank request can express that, and a full 150-document cap-length pool cannot even fit one prompt (lower bound: 150*2048 = 307,200 content tokens > max_model_len 131,072).  Equal-to-the- paper serving of depth-150 pools must replicate the block loop over POST /pooling (task token_embed): input [doc_1..doc_k, query] (the LAST item is the query) returns the projected 512-d embeds in docs-then-query order; the client chunks documents exactly like rerank(), scores each block in float32, weights blocks by max((1+cos)/2), averages the query embeds, and emits the final float32 cosines.  That loop is not expressible in the recipe schema (a product gap: no block-loop field) -- reported, not worked around. HEADROOM for that client (measured): rerank()'s capacity loop counts only document bodies, but each passage costs 13-16 wrapper+joiner prompt tokens on top of its body (the record's own averages: 13.86/document at a 63-document block, 14.28 at 150; the exact +/-1 boundary moves with BPE merges at the passage joins and the intro's passage-count digits), plus 151 fixed tokens for the record's zero-document probe render (a render that still carries both copies of its 9-token probe query; the query-free frame measures 134, and the formula's 2*q_len term reserves the query).  A client flush rule must keep 125*15 + 151 + 2*q_len + 2048 under the spare capacity (conservative: the measured worst case sits ~100 tokens lower), or vLLM refuses blocks the paper scored. Reference: the checkpoint's remote code (transformers AutoModel, auto_map, trust_remote_code=true, revision pinned) -- kind: remote_code; its environment is documented in requirements-reference.txt beside reference.py.  The reference stays faithful to the checkpoint's per-text truncation (decode-back, 2048/512 -- exactly as rerank() stages the texts) and never ports the client's cut (docs/how-to/add-a-model.md); the served client cuts verbatim prefixes against its pair budget. Both honour the anchors (the markers ride in the engine-built frame), but the over-cap cuts differ -- so the recipe declares reference.known_deviations: over_cap_cut_differs, and over-cap pairs are reported in the non-gating table while only under-cap pairs gate.  The checkpoint also sanitizes the two marker tokens out of the user text before formatting; the declared template cannot express that, so a pairs row whose query or document contains a marker literal would fail stage 1's render check by design -- keep marker literals out of evaluated inputs.  Stage 1's render check is likewise a byte comparison for pairs whose contents sit at or under the checkpoint's per-text caps (147 + 2*512 + 2048 = 3219 = the budget, so such pairs always render uncut).  A document over 2048 tokens is cut by the client at document_max_tokens and by the checkpoint decode-back, and a query over 512 tokens is settled by the client verbatim at its share while the checkpoint truncates it decode-back: both honour the caps, the boundary bytes can differ, and the harness reports every such pair (the client's processing record names the document_share or query_share cut) in the declared over_cap_cut_differs table instead of gating it.
